title: Toilet bowl fizz tabs
subtitle: Drop-in cleaning tablets for the bowl
excerpt: Small citric acid and bicarbonate tablets that fizz on contact with water, releasing peppermint and tea tree essential oils. Descale and deodorise the bowl without scrubbing. Makes 24 tabs.
sourceNotes: Citric acid and sodium bicarbonate reaction chemistry: standard general chemistry (open-access); see Wikipedia 'Citric acid' entry for reaction equations. Essential oil dispersion in water: general cosmetic formulation references.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles to 48 tablets; keep the same proportions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a batch of 24 tabs and store in an airtight jar; they last months.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps one year in a sealed, dry container. Store away from moisture; the citric acid absorbs humidity and the tablets can begin to fizz prematurely. Discard if they are already half-dissolved when you open the jar.

glossaryTerms.definition: When citric acid meets sodium bicarbonate in water, they react to produce carbon dioxide gas (the fizz), water, and sodium citrate. The CO2 scrubs surfaces as it bubbles away.

content.text: These are small pressed tablets for the toilet bowl. Drop one in, let the

work for five to ten minutes, then flush. The citric acid descales the porcelain and the bicarbonate deodorises; the essential oils leave the bowl smelling clean. One tab per week is enough for maintenance.

items.prepNote: fine; the base of the tablet
fine-ground citric acid; the acid that drives the fizz
added 2 ml at a time as a binder; just enough to hold the tablet together without triggering the fizz

content.text: Combine the bicarbonate of soda and citric acid in a dry bowl. Stir well so the two are evenly distributed. Work quickly and keep the bowl away from any steam; premature moisture triggers the fizz.
Drop the peppermint and tea tree oils into the dry mix. Stir again. The oils coat the bicarbonate crystals and help the scent carry when the tab dissolves.

Add the water 2 ml at a time, spritzing from a small spray bottle or dropping carefully with a pipette. Stir between each addition. You will see light fizzing; this is normal as long as you stop before the mix becomes wet. The mix is ready to press when it holds its shape if squeezed firmly in your hand.
Press firmly into round silicone moulds. Compact each tablet with the back of a spoon.
Leave the moulds uncovered at room temperature overnight to firm up. Unmould carefully. Store in an airtight jar as soon as the tabs are hard.

Drop one tablet into the toilet bowl. Leave for five to ten minutes while it fizzes. Brush around the bowl if needed and flush. Use once a week for maintenance; twice weekly in hard water areas where limescale builds quickly.
Keep in a sealed jar in a dry cupboard. One year shelf life when stored away from moisture and steam. Do not store on the cistern top; the humidity from the toilet degrades them.
